headline: South Asia: Saudi-led coalition strikes oil site in Yemen's capital
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Saudi-led coalition strikes oil site in Yemen's capital.
- Africa: Russia pounds Kharkiv and Lviv region with missiles and drones, killing three civilians.
- Persian Gulf Region: Iran fortifies nuclear sites, rebuilds missile arsenal as it prepares for the next war - analysis.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Army eyes changes to emergency war gear stocks amid review.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: Army eyes changes to emergency war gear stocks amid review.
The Army is nearing decisions on changes to make to its own emergency stockpiles.
- Military Times, 3 hours ago: Anduril reveals family of surface-to-air interceptor missiles.
The interceptor family was built to address threats across the air-and-missile defense spectrum, while aiming to come at a fraction of the cost of others.
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: US Army to stand up command for unmanned and autonomous warfare.
An Oct. 1 memo directs the Army vice chief of staff to establish the U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command, or FASCOM.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Constable Joel Robinson named top cop.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: Constable Joel Robinson named top cop.
Constable Joel Robinson of the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) St Catherine North Division walked away with the Chairman’s Award in the the 2026 LASCO, JCF Saluting Our Heroes Awards. Robinson, a school resource officer in the JCF’s Community Safety and Security Unit, emerged from a field of six finalists recognised for their contributions to policing and public service. His achievement also earned him a promotion to corporal, announced by Commissioner of Police Dr Kevin Blake.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: Jamaica’s tourism stature reinforced on world stage.
WESTERN BUREAU: World Travel Awards founder and president Graham Cooke has hailed Jamaica’s international tourism standing, noting that the island’s selection to host the Caribbean and Americas awards ceremony reinforces its position among the world’s leading destinations.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Southern Europe - bottom line: Ukraine had ‘no warning’ of latest Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv.
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Ukraine had ‘no warning’ of latest Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv.
Zelenskyy said intelligence sharing is "precisely what helps prevent people from being killed."
- Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: ‘A foreign attack on EU territory’: MEPs call EU to shield ICC from US sanctions.
Lawmakers ask Ursula von der Leyen to "draw a clear line towards the US administration."
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: From no cards to many: Europe warns Trump not to waste Ukraine’s leverage.
Ukraine's campaign against Russia's refineries is a growing problem for the U.S. president.
Western Russia - bottom line: Cost of insuring warehouses skyrockets in Russia following drone strikes.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Cost of insuring warehouses skyrockets in Russia following drone strikes.
Insurers in Russia have sharply raised warehouse insurance premiums following large-scale Ukrainian strikes on major storage facilities that have caused multi-billion-rouble losses for top online marketplaces.
- The Moscow Times, Balkan Insight, 7 hours ago: Bulgaria Summons Russian Ambassador After Drone Attack Sinks Ship, Leaving 11 Missing.
While Sofia has stopped short of blaming Moscow, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the drone strikes' outcome "benefits the Russian Federation."
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russia attacks Kramatorsk and Sloviansk, killing one and injuring 11 – photos.
Russian strikes have damaged homes and an office in Sloviansk; three people were injured in an attack on a charity water collection point in Kramatorsk.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russian drones "hunt" cars in Kharkiv Oblast: one killed, two injured.
A Russian drone attack damaged at least five cars in Kharkiv Oblast on 13 October, killing one person and injuring two others.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Russia pounds Kharkiv and Lviv region with missiles and drones, killing three civilians.
- Africanews, 11 hours ago: Russia pounds Kharkiv and Lviv region with missiles and drones, killing three civilians.
At least three people were killed and 37 injured in Kharkiv as Russia launched repeated aerial attacks on the north-eastern Ukrainian city on Monday and overnight. Strikes also caused damage near Lviv, in western Ukraine.
- Africanews, 10 hours ago: Sudan army chief al-Burhan orders probe into airstrike that killed 72.
Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan on Monday ordered a probe into an airstrike that killed 72 people near the Egyptian border. Rights group Emergency Lawyers accused Egypt of carrying out the strike.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 15 hours ago: Uganda: Witness Accuses Former Deputy CMI Chief Rugumayo of Torturing Him to Implicate Gen Birungi.
[Nile Post] Former ADF recruit and convicted murder suspect Hamza Lyavala has accused former Deputy Chief of Military Intelligence (CMI) Brigadier General Abdul Rugumayo of torturing him and attempting to coerce him into implicating detained General James Birungi in alleged staged bomb attacks in Kampala.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 15 hours ago: Ethiopia: Eritrean Incursions Raise Fears of a Wider Regional War in Ethiopia.
[The New Humanitarian] Addis Ababa -- Three scenarios - all grim - on how the renewed conflict in Tigray could develop.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Iran fortifies nuclear sites, rebuilds missile arsenal as it prepares for the next war - analysis.
- Jerusalem Post, 7 hours ago: Iran fortifies nuclear sites, rebuilds missile arsenal as it prepares for the next war - analysis.
The emerging picture is of an Iran continuing its efforts to rebuild its missile and drone programs despite the damage inflicted by previous US and Israeli strikes.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Netanyahu, Trump discussed possibility of renewing strikes against Iran before elections - report.
Senior US officials told Axios that Netanyahu cited alleged Iranian efforts to rebuild nuclear capacity as the reason for launching new strikes.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Booms heard in Riyadh, Aramco headquarters after Saudi coalition intercepts Houthi missiles, drones.
Saudi Civil Defense issued an early warning for the country's eastern province earlier on Tuesday, then issued another for Riyadh shortly after the interceptions.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: West Bank Palestinian family attacked by masked Jewish rioters claiming to be soldiers - report.
According to KAN, the family was at home when the rioters knocked on the door around 3 a.m., claiming to be military personnel. The settlers fled the area after the attack.
South Africa - bottom line: Zimbabwe: Mhona Appoints Board of Inquiry to Probe Lake Kariba Vessel Accident.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 10 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Mhona Appoints Board of Inquiry to Probe Lake Kariba Vessel Accident.
[263Chat] Transport and Infrastructural Development Minister Felix Mhona has appointed a three-member Board of Inquiry to investigate the circumstances surrounding a vessel casualty involving the Rural Infrastructural Development Agency (RIDA) on Lake Kariba on August 11, 2026 which killed 97 people.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Malawi: Malawi Extends Tobacco Registration Drive Ahead of New Season.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi's tobacco regulator has urged growers to begin preparations early for the 2026/27 season, warning that timely field management and adherence to recommended farming practices will be crucial to producing leaf capable of attracting stronger prices on international markets.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 8 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe Faces Fuel Cost Risks As Middle East Tensions Push Oil Prices Higher.
[263Chat] Global oil prices rose on Monday following attacks on two airports in Saudi Arabia, heightening concerns over Middle East tensions and their potential impact on fuel costs and economies, including Zimbabwe.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 8 hours ago: South Africa: Sugar Giant Tongaat Hullet Quits Stock Market As Workers Wait for Answers.
[Scrolla] About 5,800 Tongaat workers went on strike for almost four weeks and won 6%, backdated to April. Six strike days are paid. Tongaat's emergency funding ended on 30 September and no extension is known. It leaves the stock exchange on 3 November.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Saudi-led coalition strikes oil site in Yemen's capital.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, South China Morning Post - China, just now: Saudi-led coalition strikes oil site in Yemen's capital.
Yemen’s Houthis said Saudi Arabia struck an oil facility in Sanaa on Tuesday, after the Riyadh-led coalition told civilians to leave the surrounding area in its first evacuation order for the Yemeni capital since the war flared up again. The Saudi-led coalition said military operations were conducted against “vital assets” used by the Houthis to wage war in Yemen.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: Pakistan condemns Israeli actions in Syria, calls for withdrawal.
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has condemned continued Israeli military actions in Syria, calling for Israel’s withdrawal from all occupied Syrian territory and full respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. Speaking at a UN Security Council briefing on the humanitarian and political situation in Syria on Monday evening, Pakistan’s Acting Permanent Representative, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, said Israeli actions violated international law and Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, undermining prospects for regional peace and stability.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: 'We're not giving up': Activist Thunberg joins France student protests.
Thousands of protesters marched through central Paris on Tuesday as part of nationwide demonstrations supporting high school pupils who have been protesting for better classroom conditions, with Swedish activist Greta Thunberg taking part. With just six months to go before elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron, French authorities had been hoping that the protests were easing ahead of half-term holidays starting at the end of this week.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Kusal Mendis' blistering 87 leads Sri Lanka to consolation win over Pakistan in third T20I.
Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis produced a blistering unbeaten 87 off 48 balls to steer the visitors to an eight-wicket consolation victory over Pakistan in the third Twenty20 International at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday. Chasing 169, Sri Lanka cruised to 172-2 in 17.1 overs, with Kusal and Kamindu Mendis combining in an unbroken 98-run partnership for the third wicket to complete the chase with 17 balls to spare. Kamindu remained unbeaten on 40 off 27 deliveries, striking four fours, as Sri Lanka ended the series on a winning note after Pakistan had secured the first two matches.
Asia - bottom line: Could Pakistan’s Chinese-made weapons help protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks?.
- South China Morning Post - China, 7 hours ago: Could Pakistan’s Chinese-made weapons help protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks?.
Chinese-Pakistani fighter jets and a China-made air-defence system reportedly deployed to Saudi Arabia could be brought into action following Pakistan’s renewed pledge to defend the kingdom after deadly Houthi attacks on Riyadh. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Sunday that Islamabad would cooperate with Riyadh “in every possible way” under their defence agreements, after Houthi strikes on the Saudi capital’s main airport the previous day killed at least 13 people and wounded...
- South China Morning Post - China, 12 hours ago: North Korea’s new missile museum: part shrine, part arms bazaar.
North Korea now has a museum for its bombs. The National Defence Revolution Museum, which opened on Sunday, is the country’s first dedicated exclusively to military hardware, from rifles to intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs). Observers say it is also intended to send a message to Washington and Seoul, serve as a permanent showroom for the North’s arms exports and visibly enshrine its nuclear programme as an irreversible part of state policy. Third-generation ruler Kim Jong-un cut the...
- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 4 hours ago: MI5 chief warns Iran is targeting military sites in UK as hostile state threats surge.
Iran is trying to hit military sites in the UK and the suspected plot to attack a US-run military airbase in September was “not unique”, the head of Britain’s MI5 spy agency said on Tuesday. Ken McCallum, who leads the UK’s domestic security service, said Tehran was seeking to intensify its attacks in Britain beyond the traditional targets of Iranians opposed to the country’s Islamic authorities. That has included arson and sabotage attacks on Jewish sites that Britain says were carried out by...
- Taipei Times, just now: Government slams strikes on main airport in Riyadh.
India - bottom line: 18 Deaths, 2 Dozen Strikes, 15,000 sqkm Lost: A Month Of Houthi-Saudi War.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: 18 Deaths, 2 Dozen Strikes, 15,000 sqkm Lost: A Month Of Houthi-Saudi War.
Data compiled by NDTV Datafy shows that since September 7, the Houthis have carried out at least two dozen major attacks on Saudi airports, oil refineries, pipelines, gas processing and storage sites, and military installations.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: New Jersey couple’s viral homeless veteran story raised $400,000; it was fabricated.
Katelyn McClure and Mark D'Amico launched a heartfelt campaign to support Johnny Bobbitt Jr, a homeless veteran, asserting that he heroically assisted McClure during a fuel mishap. This poignant story garnered around $400,000 from over 14,000 donors, who were unaware of the deception. Upon investigation, it was revealed that the couple misappropriated the contributions for lavish purchases while Bobbitt pursued legal recourse for his funds.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Mumbai Airport Says Airlines To Operate Winter Flight As Planned.
The meeting between Mumbai International Airport Limited (MIAL), airlines and the ministry on Tuesday ended on a positive note, with both sides agreeing to work towards a plan for the redevelopment of Terminal 1
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Several Children Among 13 Killed As Boat Overturns In Ganga In Bihar.
"I pray for the speedy recovery of all those injured," said Prime Minister Narendra Modi while announcing financial relief of Rs 2 lakh for the families of the victims.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Kim Jong Un opens new weapons museum as North Korea claims missile test success.
- NK News, 21 hours ago: Kim Jong Un opens new weapons museum as North Korea claims missile test success.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un opened a new arms museum to showcase the country’s nuclear missiles, drones and other weapons, vowing to continue their development, according to state media. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) separately published a brief report on Monday’s missile test, claiming it heralded “an important change” in improving all weapons […]
- Yonhap News Agency, 2 hours ago: N. Korea gaining experience in troop deployment, sustaining military operations through Ukraine war: USFK chief.
WASHINGTON, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- North Korea is gaining experience in deploying t...
- Yonhap News Agency, 14 hours ago: (LEAD) Arms agency to accelerate development of nuclear-powered subs, AI-driven combat systems.
SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- The arms procurement agency said Tuesday it will spee...
- Yonhap News Agency, 17 hours ago: (LEAD) USFK chief calls for more dispersed military drills across S. Korea, citing Ukraine war lessons.
WASHINGTON/SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- The commander of U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) ...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Blasts rock Yemen's capital as Houthis vow to retaliate.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Blasts rock Yemen's capital as Houthis vow to retaliate.
The strikes mark a fresh escalation in the widening Middle East crisis, with Yemen's Houthis vowing to retaliate with attacks on Saudi Arabia's airports and oil refineries.
- The Guardian - Australia, 5 hours ago: Family and sexual violence rates against Australian children rise sharply as researchers warn of ‘manosphere’.
Study authors say increase cannot be attributed to any one factor and list income inequality and reporting increases due to growing awareness as other likely reasons Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The sexual assault of Australian children has accelerated sharply since the pandemic, surprising researchers who expected rates to have fallen but instead found attacks on boys had risen 15.7%. Researchers expected rates to have dropped in line with other countries around the world and warn the troubling findings show an urgent need to prevent the suffering of children.
- The Guardian - Australia, just now: Australian politics live: Chalmers urges against mocking, cancelling or talking down to One Nation supporters.
Follow the day’s news live. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Forecasts suggest ‘cautious confidence’ in the economy, says Chalmers In the wake of the IMF report warning of a “clear and present danger” to the world economy, Chalmers said that Treasury and Reserve Bank forecasts suggest some “cautious confidence” is appropriate on things getting better, and as a result, helping the standing of Labor against One Nation. They don’t expect things to get a lot better in the next 12 weeks but they do expect things to get a bit better over the next 12 months.
- The Guardian - Australia, just now: Morning Mail: AFL tells Sportsbet to ditch AI players; Anne Aly reveals death threats; and Musk’s electoral play.
Want to get this in your inbox every weekday? Sign up for the Morning Mail here, and finish your day with our Politics, really newsletter. Morning everyone. Our exclusive lead story reveals how the AFL has told its commercial partner, Sportsbet, to stop promoting its products with AI-generated images and memes of players without their consent.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
